title: A meta systematic review of artificial intelligence in higher education: a call for increased ethics, collaboration, and rigour
venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education
extended_summary:
This paper is a tertiary review (review of reviews) that maps the scope, quality, and characteristics of artificial intelligence in higher education (AIHEd) evidence syntheses published between 2018 and mid-2023. The authors ask what kinds of evidence syntheses are being conducted, where they are published, who is producing them, what AI applications they focus on, and how rigorously they are reported. The motivation is to reduce research waste and provide a clearer foundation for future AI research and policy in higher education.

The study does not evaluate a single AI intervention. Instead, it synthesizes 66 secondary studies that themselves reviewed primary AI research in formal higher-education and continuing-education settings. The corpus includes systematic reviews, scoping reviews, meta-analyses, mapping reviews, bibliometric reviews, and related evidence syntheses. The reviewed primary literature covers applications such as adaptive systems and personalization, profiling and prediction, assessment and evaluation, and intelligent tutoring systems. The most common settings and populations discussed are higher-education learners, especially undergraduate and graduate/doctoral students, along with some studies involving institutional and administrative functions.

The main conclusions are that AIHEd evidence synthesis has grown rapidly, is mostly collaborative, and is concentrated in systematic reviews, but methodological reporting quality is uneven. Many reviews fail to report inter-rater reliability, exact coding schemes, full quality appraisal, or reflections on limitations. The field is heavily oriented toward learner-facing applications, while administrative uses are less common. The authors call for greater methodological rigor, better ethics and transparency, and stronger interdisciplinary collaboration in future AI in education research.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: An intelligent tutoring system is an AI-driven educational system that supports instruction through guided learning, diagnosis, and automated feedback, often adapting to learner needs.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper is a tertiary review of AI in higher education and includes intelligent tutoring systems as one of the main application categories, but it does not evaluate a specific ITS product or primary study directly.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a tertiary review of secondary studies, not a primary evaluation of an AI tool. It does not provide direct experimental evidence on a specific tool in the target K–12 teacher coaching or lesson-feedback domain.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct outcome effect is reported for a specific tool, and the paper is not an intervention study. Its findings are descriptive about the state of the literature rather than impacts on teacher practice or student outcomes.
